  "repair_strategy": "Modify syncState to only apply aria-hidden when the menu button is actually visible (offsetParent non‑null), preserving the navigation's accessibility state on desktop while retaining the existing behavior for the mobile menu.",

Header.prototype.syncState = function (isVisible) {
  this.$menuButton.classList.toggle('govuk-header__menu-button--open', isVisible)
  this.$menuButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', isVisible)
  this.$menu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', !isVisible)
}",
      "after": "/**
 * Sync menu state
 *
 * Sync the menu button class and the accessible state of the menu and the menu
 * button with the visible state of the menu
 *
 * @param {boolean} isVisible Whether the menu is currently visible
 */
Header.prototype.syncState = function (isVisible) {
  this.$menuButton.classList.toggle('govuk-header__menu-button--open', isVisible)
  this.$menuButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', isVisible)
  if (this.$menuButton.offsetParent) {
    this.$menu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', !isVisible)
  }
}"
    }
  ],
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Navigation links will be exposed in the accessibility tree as links with correct names, allowing keyboard and screen‑reader users to reach them.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "If the menu button becomes visible via other means (e.g., custom styling), aria‑hidden may not be updated correctly.",
    "Changing the conditional logic could affect edge cases where offsetParent is null but the menu is still visible (unlikely)."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "After page load at desktop width, inspect the navigation ul and verify it has no aria-hidden attribute (or aria-hidden='false').",
    "Tabbing from the home link should move focus to the 'Apply' link and the accessibility tree should show role link with name 'Apply'.",
    "Resizing to mobile width and opening the menu should still hide/show the navigation correctly and update aria‑hidden appropriately."
  ]
}

Observed failure: Expected state did not occur after action step=0 where seeking selector "#nav-apply". After pressing Tab? Actually journey: seek element #nav-apply, assert ax name "Apply" role link fails because observed 0 meaning maybe AX tree didn't expose as link? In DOM we saw anchor tag but perhaps due to being inside hidden nav? Wait initial state: navigation list is present but aria-hidden="true"? Let's check index.html snippet: It shows:

<nav>
  <ul id="navigation" class="govuk-header__navigation" aria-label="Navigation menu">
...
No aria-hidden attribute! But earlier in observed 'before' body includes same markup without aria-hidden. However later after some steps? The observed after still same. So why assertion failed? Possibly because the component script adds aria-hidden when JS enabled? Indeed body class "js-enabled". The header component likely hides navigation on small screens via JS toggling class and setting aria-hidden based on visibility. On desktop width (>40em), the navigation should be visible and aria-hidden false? Let's examine component code: It toggles class 'govuk-header__navigation--open' on menu button click, and syncState sets aria-expanded on button and aria-hidden on menu opposite of isVisible. Initially, syncState called with isVisible = this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open'). On page load, does navigation have that class? No. So isVisible false. Then syncState sets aria-expanded false (button) and aria-hidden true (menu). That means on desktop, navigation is incorrectly hidden from assistive tech! The CSS shows navigation displayed as inline-block items regardless of JS? Actually CSS: .govuk-header__navigation {margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none}. .govuk-header__navigation-item {display:inline-block;margin-right:15px;padding:5px 0}. There's no media query hiding it. The JS only affects small screens (<40em) where menu button display:none becomes inline-block and navigation hidden via JS. But on desktop, menu button is display:none (since .govuk-header__menu-button{display:none}) and navigation is visible. However the JS still sets aria-hidden true regardless of viewport, causing accessibility failure.

Thus fix: In init, we should set initial isVisible based on whether navigation is visually visible (i.e., not hidden by CSS). Simpler: For desktop, we should not set aria-hidden true; we should reflect actual visibility. Since menu button is hidden on desktop, we could skip setting aria-hidden when menu button is not present? Actually menu button exists but is hidden via CSS display:none. The component should not manipulate aria-hidden when menu button is not displayed (i.e., when $menuButton.offsetParent !== null?). Or we can compute isVisible = !$menu.hasAttribute('hidden')? Not.

Simplest: Remove the line that sets aria-hidden on menu in syncState, or set it based on isVisible but also ensure that when menu button is hidden (desktop), we keep aria-hidden false. Actually we want navigation to be accessible always when visible. Since menu button is hidden on desktop, we could treat isVisible = true when menu button is not displayed (i.e., !$menuButton.offsetParent). Let's implement: In syncState, compute isVisible = arguments[0] ?? (this.$menuButton ? !this.$menuButton.classList.contains('govuk-header__menu-button--open') : true)? Hmm.

Better approach: Only set aria-hidden when the menu button is present and visible (i.e., not display:none). If menu button is hidden (desktop), we should not modify aria-hidden (leave default false). So in syncState, we can check if this.$menuButton.offsetParent !== null (meaning it's not hidden). If hidden, skip setting aria-hidden.

Original header.js content:

import '../../vendor/polyfills/Event'
import '../../vendor/polyfills/Element/prototype/classList'
import '../../vendor/polyfills/Function/prototype/bind'

function Header ($module) {
  this.$module = $module
  this.$menuButton = $module && $module.querySelector('.govuk-js-header-toggle')
  this.$menu = this.$menuButton && $module.querySelector(
    '#' + this.$menuButton.getAttribute('aria-controls')
  )
}

/**
 * Initialise header
 *
 * Check for the presence of the header, menu and menu button – if any are
 * missing then there's nothing to do so return early.
 */
Header.prototype.init = function () {
  if (!this.$module || !this.$menuButton || !this.$menu) {
    return
  }

  this.syncState(this.$menu.classList.contains('govuk-header__navigation--open'))
  this.$menuButton.addEventListener('click', this.handleMenuButtonClick.bind(this))
}

/**
 * Sync menu state
 *
 * Sync the menu button class and the accessible state of the menu and the menu
 * button with the visible state of the menu
 *
 * @param {boolean} isVisible Whether the menu is currently visible
 */
Header.prototype.syncState = function (isVisible) {
  this.$menuButton.classList.toggle('govuk-header__menu-button--open', isVisible)
  this.$menuButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', isVisible)
  this.$menu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', !isVisible)
}

/**
 * Handle menu button click
 *
 * When the menu button is clicked, change the visibility of the menu and then
 * sync the accessibility state and menu button state
 */
Header.prototype.handleMenuButtonClick = function () {
  var isVisible = this.$menu.classList.toggle('govuk-header__navigation--open')
  this.syncState(isVisible)
}

export default Header

We need to modify syncState to conditionally set aria-hidden only when menu button is not hidden (i.e., when it's visible). Determine visibility: this.$menuButton.offsetParent !== null (or getComputedStyle). We'll add:

if (this.$menuButton.offsetParent) {
  this.$menu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', !isVisible)
}
// else do nothing (leave attribute as is)

Also ensure we don't remove aria-hidden attribute when hidden? Might leave previous value; but on desktop initially it will have no aria-hidden attribute (default false). Good.

/**
